name: National Scholarship Portal
summary: Government single-window platform for discovering, applying for and tracking eligible scholarships.
eligibility: Eligibility is scholarship-specific and can depend on state, course, category, income and other criteria.
benefits: Scholarship assistance according to the selected scholarship's rules.
steps: Search the relevant scholarship
Check current eligibility and requirements
Complete registration/OTR if required
Apply and upload documents
Track application/payment status
source: National Scholarship Portal / National Government Services Portal

name: MahaDBT Post-Matric Scholarships
summary: Maharashtra's Aaple Sarkar DBT portal provides access to multiple post-matric scholarship, freeship and education-benefit schemes.
eligibility: Criteria vary by department and scheme; the portal provides an eligibility finder using fields such as qualification, address, income, department and disability.
benefits: Tuition/examination fee support, maintenance allowance or other education benefits depending on the selected scheme.
steps: Use Find Eligible Schemes
Select the applicable scheme
Read the scheme's eligibility and documents
Register/login
Submit and track the application
source: MahaDBT official portal

name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
summary: A credit-linked government programme that supports eligible individuals in setting up new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector and promotes self-employment and employment generation.
eligibility: For new enterprises, an individual above 18 years can apply. There is no income ceiling. For projects above ₹10 lakh in manufacturing or ₹5 lakh in business/service, the applicant must have at least an VIII-standard pass qualification. Only new eligible projects are covered.
benefits: Financial assistance through bank-linked credit and margin-money subsidy for eligible new micro-enterprises, subject to the applicable PMEGP guidelines.
documents: Other documents required by the PMEGP application process
steps: Check PMEGP eligibility and project conditions
Prepare a business/project proposal
Apply through the official PMEGP portal
Complete verification and bank appraisal
Complete the required training/formalities
Track the application and loan/subsidy status
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises / KVIC / PMEGP official portal

name: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA)
summary: A rural employment programme that provides a legal guarantee of wage employment to rural households whose adult members volunteer to perform unskilled manual work.
eligibility: An Indian citizen who is 18 years or older and resides in a rural area can apply for work under MGNREGA. Employment is provided to rural households according to the scheme's demand-driven process and applicable rules.
benefits: A legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment per rural household in a financial year, along with rural asset creation and livelihood-supporting works.
documents: Bank or postal account details for wage payments where applicable
steps: Approach the local Gram Panchayat
Request registration for the household and obtain a Job Card
Submit a demand for work
Receive work allocation according to the programme process
Complete the assigned work
Check attendance, wages and payment status through the official system
source: Ministry of Rural Development / Mahatma Gandhi NREGA official portal

name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
summary: A Ministry of Rural Development skilling programme focused on rural youth from poor families, with training linked to employability and career opportunities.
eligibility: The programme primarily targets rural youth from poor families between 15 and 35 years of age, subject to the current programme guidelines and state implementation rules.
benefits: Skill training, certification and employment-oriented support designed to improve the income opportunities and career prospects of eligible rural youth.
documents: Other documents requested by the authorised training provider
steps: Check DDU-GKY eligibility
Find an authorised DDU-GKY training opportunity
Select a suitable course/training programme
Complete registration and verification
Attend the required training
Complete assessment/certification and follow the programme's placement process
source: Ministry of Rural Development / DDU-GKY official portal

name: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
tags: Micro-Credit • Street Vendors & Hawkers • Urban Livelihood • Self-Employed Youth & Vendors
summary: Affordable collateral-free working capital micro-loans designed to empower urban and peri-urban street vendors to resume and expand daily operations.
eligibility: Urban street vendors in possession of a Certificate of Vending or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) issued by the local Municipal Body / Town Vending Committee (TVC). Eligibility is also governed by current PM SVANidhi guidelines and vendor verification requirements.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loan of ₹10,000 in the first tranche. Loan escalating to ₹20,000 and ₹50,000 upon timely repayment. 7% interest subsidy. Up to ₹1,200 annual digital transaction cashback.
documents: Certificate of Vending or ULB Letter of Recommendation (LoR)
steps: Verify your name in the local Town Vending Committee survey
Open the official PM SVANidhi portal or visit a Common Service Centre (CSC)
Authenticate your mobile number via Aadhaar OTP
Choose your preferred lending bank/NBFC and submit the e-application
Undergo verification by the Urban Local Body and receive credit directly via DBT
source: MoHUA / PM SVANidhi official portal

name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
summary: Income-support scheme for eligible landholding farmer families subject to scheme exclusions.
eligibility: The official PM-KISAN guidelines define eligible landholding farmer families and exclusion categories; beneficiaries are identified by States/UTs.
benefits: ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments, subject to current scheme rules.
documents: eKYC/other details required by the official process
steps: Check eligibility and exclusions
Complete farmer registration/status checks
Complete mandatory eKYC where required
Verify bank/beneficiary details
Track instalments/status
source: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / PM-KISAN

name: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana
summary: Financial-inclusion programme providing access to basic banking and linked financial services.
eligibility: A basic savings bank deposit account can be opened by a person who does not have another account, subject to the bank's current account-opening requirements.
benefits: Basic savings account, no minimum balance requirement, RuPay debit card and access to linked financial services subject to applicable rules.
documents: Other bank account-opening information as required
steps: Visit a bank branch or authorised Bank Mitra
Provide required KYC information
Open the account
Ask about eligible linked services
source: Department of Financial Services / PMJDY

name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
summary: Renewable one-year life-insurance scheme for eligible subscribers.
eligibility: Official scheme information states eligibility for individuals aged 18–50 with a participating savings bank or post-office account, subject to current rules.
benefits: Life cover of ₹2 lakh for death due to any reason, subject to current scheme terms.
steps: Review current scheme terms
Approach participating bank/post office
Complete enrolment/consent
Keep nominee details updated
source: Department of Financial Services / Jan Suraksha — PMJJBY

name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana
summary: Renewable one-year personal-accident insurance scheme for eligible subscribers.
eligibility: Official scheme information states eligibility for individuals aged 18–70 with a participating bank/post-office account, subject to current rules.
benefits: Accidental death/total disability cover of ₹2 lakh and partial disability cover of ₹1 lakh, subject to scheme terms.
steps: Review current scheme terms
Approach participating bank/post office
Complete enrolment/consent
Keep nominee details updated
source: Department of Financial Services / Jan Suraksha — PMSBY official form

name: Atal Pension Yojana
summary: Government-supported pension scheme for eligible subscribers with a savings bank/post-office account.
eligibility: Open to citizens of India aged 18–40 with a savings bank/post-office account, subject to current rules; income-tax payers are excluded from joining under the current rule cited by the official scheme document.
benefits: Guaranteed minimum pension options after age 60 according to the subscriber's chosen contribution/pension option and scheme rules.
steps: Check current eligibility
Approach participating bank/post office
Select pension option and contribution frequency
Complete enrolment/consent
Maintain contributions
source: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) / APY

name: Shravanbal Seva Rajya Nivruttivetan Yojana
summary: A Maharashtra Government pension scheme that provides monthly financial assistance to eligible elderly persons.
eligibility: Eligible elderly individuals aged 65 years and above whose names are on the Below Poverty Line (BPL) list or whose annual income is less than ₹21,000, subject to applicable government rules and verification.
benefits: ₹1,500 per month in financial assistance to each eligible beneficiary.
documents: Income certificate or BPL details where applicable
steps: Check the current eligibility criteria
Visit the official Maharashtra Special Assistance portal for scheme information
Check the required application process
Apply through the prescribed Collector's Office, Tehsildar's Office, Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana Branch or Talathi Office
Complete verification as required
Track the benefit/status through the applicable official system
source: Government of Maharashtra / Social Justice & Special Assistance Department

name: PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS)
tags: Education & Scholarship • Higher Education Pursuing Youth
summary: A merit-cum-means scholarship from the Ministry of Education for meritorious students pursuing higher education at colleges and universities across India, to help meet day-to-day expenses during their studies.
eligibility: Students who scored above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their relevant stream in Class XII from a recognised Board; enrolled in a regular (non-correspondence/distance) undergraduate or postgraduate course at a college or university; family income from all sources not exceeding ₹4.5 lakh per annum; not receiving any other scholarship or fee reimbursement. Diploma students and students who took a gap year after Class XII are not eligible.
benefits: ₹10,000 per annum for the first three years of undergraduate study, and ₹20,000 per annum for postgraduate and professional degree courses (e.g. Medical, Engineering). Scholarship is disbursed directly to the student's bank account through DBT via the National Scholarship Portal.
documents: Class XII mark sheet (for fresh applicants) or latest mark sheet (for renewal)
Family income certificate issued by a competent authority
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in
Select 'Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (PM-USP CSSS)' under Central Schemes
Fill in the application with academic, personal, and income details
Upload required documents
Submit before the closing date announced on NSP
Track application and payment status through the NSP dashboard
source: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education / National Scholarship Portal

name: SWAYAM — Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
summary: A Government of India platform offering free online courses taught by faculty from premier institutions (IITs, IIMs, central universities and others) covering school, undergraduate, postgraduate, and professional levels. Learners can earn certificates and, through their university, transfer up to 40% of semester credits via SWAYAM courses as per UGC regulations.
eligibility: Open to anyone — there is no age, income, or educational qualification requirement for enrolling in courses. Any learner can register and access course content for free. To earn a proctored certificate, learners must register for the end-term exam (a fee applies) and meet the minimum marks criteria set by the course.
benefits: Free access to high-quality course content from top institutions. Proctored certificates on passing the exam. Academic credit transfer of up to 40% of semester courses as per UGC Credit Framework, subject to the learner's university policy. Supports lifelong learning and skill development.
documents: No additional documents required to access or enrol in courses
steps: Visit swayam.gov.in and create a free learner account
Browse or search for a course by subject, level, or institution
Enrol in the desired course — all content is free
Complete course assignments and watch video lectures
Register for the proctored exam (paid, optional) if a certificate is desired
Check with your college/university about credit transfer procedures for SWAYAM courses
source: Ministry of Education / SWAYAM — Government of India

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girl Students
summary: An AICTE scholarship to support girl students pursuing technical education (degree or diploma) at AICTE-approved institutions, encouraging women to enter and complete technical courses.
eligibility: Girl students admitted to the first year of an AICTE-approved degree (B.E./B.Tech/B.Arch/etc.) or diploma programme; family income from all sources not exceeding ₹8 lakh per annum; maximum two girls per family are eligible; not receiving any other government scholarship simultaneously.
benefits: Up to ₹50,000 per annum per student, covering tuition fee up to ₹30,000 or at actuals, whichever is less, plus ₹2,000 per month for 10 months as incidentals (totalling ₹20,000). Disbursed annually for the duration of the course subject to maintaining eligibility.
documents: Admission letter / college enrolment proof from an AICTE-approved institution
Family income certificate issued by a State/UT government authority
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in
Select AICTE Pragati Scholarship under Central Schemes
Complete the application with personal, academic, and income details
Upload required documents
Submit the application before the advertised deadline
Track application and disbursement status on the NSP portal
source: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) / National Scholarship Portal

name: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)
summary: A Department of Science and Technology (DST) scholarship that encourages talented students to pursue natural and basic sciences at the undergraduate and postgraduate level, building a strong base of science researchers in India.
eligibility: Students who secured aggregate marks within the top 1% in their Class XII examination from any State or Central Board and are pursuing (or have been admitted to) a Bachelor's or Master's programme in natural or basic sciences (B.Sc./B.S./Int. M.Sc./M.S. or equivalent) at a recognised institution. Students admitted through JEE, NEET, KVPY, and Olympiad routes are also eligible through specific channels.
benefits: ₹80,000 per annum (₹6,667 per month) for up to five years of undergraduate and postgraduate study in natural/basic sciences. Also includes a summer attachment programme with research institutions.
documents: Class XII mark sheet or board certificate as proof of eligibility
Class X mark sheet or certificate as proof of date of birth
Admission/enrolment proof from the institution (B.Sc./M.Sc. or equivalent)
Valid email address for portal registration
Other documents as required by the online application form
steps: Register on the INSPIRE portal at online-inspire.gov.in
Select 'Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)' and complete the application
Upload Class XII mark sheet, Class X certificate, and admission proof
Submit the application before the advertised deadline
Applications are screened internally, followed by final selection by an Expert Committee
Results and offer letters are communicated through the INSPIRE web-portal account
source: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India / INSPIRE Portal

name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS)
summary: A central government scholarship to arrest the dropout of meritorious students from economically weaker sections at Class VIII and support them to continue their secondary and higher secondary education.
eligibility: Students studying in Class VIII in State Government, Government-aided, or local body schools; family income from all sources not exceeding ₹3.5 lakh per annum; must qualify the State-level NMMSS examination (MAT + SAT with a minimum of 40% aggregate, or 32% for SC/ST students); must secure at least 55% marks in Class VII (50% for SC/ST). Private school students and students attending central government schools (Navodaya, KVS, Sainik, etc.) are not eligible.
benefits: ₹12,000 per annum (₹1,000 per month) for study in Classes IX to XII, subject to continuation and renewal criteria. Disbursed directly to the student's bank account through DBT.
documents: Income certificate issued by a competent authority (showing income ≤ ₹3.5 lakh per annum)
State NMMSS examination admit card and score card
steps: Check eligibility and apply for the State-level NMMSS examination through your school or State Education Board
Qualify the MAT and SAT examination with the required minimum marks
Register on the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in
Select 'National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme' and complete the application
Upload income certificate and other required documents
Submit before the advertised deadline and track status on NSP
source: Department of School Education & Literacy (DSEL), Ministry of Education / NSP

name: National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)
summary: A Ministry of Education scheme under the Apprentices Act, 1961, that provides practical on-the-job training to fresh engineering graduates, diploma holders, and vocational certificate holders with participating industries across India, bridging the gap between academic knowledge and industry skills.
eligibility: Fresh graduates (B.E./B.Tech or equivalent) and diploma holders from recognised institutions who have not yet undergone apprenticeship training under NATS. Typically for candidates who have completed their degree or diploma and are looking for practical industry exposure. Vocational certificate holders in relevant fields are also eligible.
benefits: Stipend paid by the employer (minimum rates prescribed by the government, revised from April 2026). On-the-job training of 6 months to 1 year at a registered establishment. Certificate of Apprenticeship Training on completion, issued by BOAT/BOPT. Government shares part of the stipend cost for eligible apprentices through DBT.
documents: Mark sheets from the qualifying examination
Bank account details for DBT stipend
steps: Register as a student/graduate on the NATS portal at nats.education.gov.in
Complete the profile with academic details and preferences
Search for apprenticeship vacancies listed by registered establishments
Apply to a suitable vacancy and await selection by the establishment
Complete the apprenticeship contract formalities on the portal
Undergo the training period and collect the apprenticeship certificate on completion
source: Board of Apprenticeship and Training (BOAT/BOPT) / Ministry of Education, Government of India

name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)
summary: A Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship scheme that promotes apprenticeship training in India by sharing the cost of stipend with employers and supporting basic training, making it easier for establishments to hire and train apprentices under the Apprentices Act.
eligibility: Any employer registered under the Apprentices Act can participate. Apprentices must be at least 14 years of age and meet the educational qualification prescribed for the relevant trade. The stipend-sharing benefit applies to apprentices engaged by eligible establishments through the official apprenticeship portal.
benefits: Government reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend per apprentice per month, subject to a maximum of ₹1,500 per month per apprentice. Additionally, basic training cost is shared with Basic Training Providers up to ₹7,500 (one-time, for 500 hours / 3 months) per eligible trainee. This reduces the financial burden on employers and encourages wider apprenticeship engagement.
documents: Apprentice: Age proof and educational qualification certificate
Apprentice: Bank account details for stipend DBT
steps: Employers register their establishment on the Apprenticeship Portal at apprenticeship.gov.in
Post apprenticeship vacancies and select candidates
Register the apprentice and file the apprenticeship contract on the portal
Apprentice undergoes on-the-job training as per the trade curriculum
Employer claims stipend reimbursement through the portal after each pay period
Apprentice receives government share of stipend through DBT into their bank account
source: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship / Apprenticeship India Portal

name: National Career Service (NCS) Portal
summary: A free digital platform from the Ministry of Labour and Employment that connects job seekers with employers across India. It offers job listings in both private and government sectors, career counselling, psychometric assessments, details of career centres, and information on job fairs and employment events.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen seeking employment or career guidance can register as a job seeker on NCS free of charge. Employers, organisations, and career centres can also register. There is no income or qualification barrier for registration.
benefits: Free access to job listings across government and private sectors. Psychometric and aptitude assessment tools to guide career choices. Information about upcoming job fairs and career events. Ability to connect with career centres in your district. NCS does not charge any fee at any stage of registration, job application, or employment-related services.
documents: Valid mobile number and email address for registration
Aadhaar or other identity proof (optional, for enhanced profile)
steps: Visit the NCS portal at ncs.gov.in
Register as a job seeker using your mobile number and email
Complete your profile with education, skills, and work experience
Search for jobs by keyword, location, sector, or qualification
Apply directly to listed vacancies through the portal
Use the Assessment Tool for career guidance and visit listed Career Centres if needed
source: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India / NCS Portal

name: PM Vishwakarma
summary: A Central Sector Scheme launched in September 2023 to provide end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople working in 18 identified trades, helping them improve the quality and reach of their products and integrate into formal economic value chains.
eligibility: An artisan or craftsperson aged 18 years or above engaged in one of the 18 specified family-based traditional trades in the unorganised sector on a self-employment basis. The applicant should not be enrolled in similar central government credit-based schemes (PMEGP, PM SVANidhi, Mudra). One member per family is eligible. The 18 trades include: Carpenter, Boat Maker, Armourer, Blacksmith, Hammer & Tool Kit Maker, Locksmith, Goldsmith, Potter, Sculptor/Stone Carver, Cobbler, Mason (Raajmistri), Basket/Mat/Broom Maker, Doll & Toy Maker, Barber, Garland Maker, Washerman, Tailor, and Fishing Net Maker.
benefits: PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card. Skill training: 5-day basic training and 15+ day advanced training with a stipend of ₹500 per day during training. Toolkit incentive grant of ₹15,000 (disbursed through e-RUPI). Collateral-free credit support: loan up to ₹1 lakh (first tranche) and up to ₹2 lakh (second tranche) at a concessional interest rate of 5% (government bears the interest subvention cap). Digital transaction incentives and market linkage support.
documents: Proof of trade practice (as part of registration verification at Common Service Centre)
steps: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) for registration — online registration is done through CSC operators
Undergo skill verification for your trade
Receive PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card
Attend basic skill training (5 days) and collect toolkit incentive of ₹15,000
Optionally enrol for advanced training (15+ days)
Apply for collateral-free credit through a participating bank or financial institution
Track benefits and status at pmvishwakarma.gov.in
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India / PM Vishwakarma Portal

name: Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI)
summary: A Ministry of Rural Development initiative under DAY-NRLM to establish dedicated skill-training and entrepreneurship-development institutes in every district of India, providing free residential training to rural youth — particularly from BPL households — to help them start self-employment ventures.
eligibility: Rural youth, primarily from Below Poverty Line (BPL) or low-income rural households. Preference is given to beneficiaries of DAY-NRLM SHGs and family members of MGNREGA job-card holders. Minimum educational qualification varies by course. Age is typically 18–45 years, though this may vary by RSETI and programme.
benefits: Free residential skill training at a district-level RSETI centre (managed by lead banks sponsored by the government). Training is followed by handholding and credit linkage support to help trainees start their own enterprises. Completion certificate recognised for bank credit linkage. Settlement rate of at least 70% is mandated for RSETIs.
documents: BPL/income proof or NRLM SHG membership details (if applicable)
Educational qualification certificate (as required by the specific course)
steps: Identify the RSETI centre in your district through rseti.in or the local block/Gram Panchayat office
Enquire about upcoming training programmes and enrolment dates
Submit your application and documents to the RSETI centre
Attend the free residential training programme
Receive settlement support and credit linkage assistance from the RSETI after training
Follow up with the RSETI for handholding support to set up your enterprise
source: Ministry of Rural Development / DAY-NRLM / RSETI India

name: NIELIT Digital Literacy & IT Certification Courses
summary: The National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), offers a range of government-certified digital literacy and IT courses — from basic computer awareness to advanced IT certifications — helping citizens and professionals build digital skills through its centres across India.
eligibility: Eligibility varies by course level. Basic digital literacy courses such as BCC (Basic Computer Course) and CCC (Course on Computer Concepts) are open to anyone regardless of educational qualification. Higher-level IT and electronics courses require a relevant educational background as specified for each course. SC/ST candidates and persons with disabilities may receive fee concessions as per current guidelines.
benefits: Government-recognised certificates from NIELIT/MeitY that are accepted for government jobs and other purposes. Affordable, structured courses ranging from basic digital literacy (BCC, CCC, CCC+, ECC) to advanced IT and electronics programmes. Availability at NIELIT centres across India and through approved private training institutes.
documents: Educational qualification certificate (as required by the specific course)
Caste/disability certificate (if applicable, for fee concession)
steps: Visit the NIELIT website at nielit.gov.in and check available courses and current admission notices
Select a course suitable for your qualification and goals
Apply online through the NIELIT admission portal at onlineapply.nielit.in
Complete registration, upload required documents, and pay the course fee online
Attend classes at a NIELIT centre or approved institute (as applicable)
Register for and appear in the examination to receive the NIELIT certificate
source: National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) / MeitY, Government of India

name: Stand-Up India
audience: SC/ST and Women Entrepreneurs / Youth / Business / Vendor
tags: Greenfield Credit • SC/ST & Women Business Owners • Business & Livelihood
summary: A Ministry of Finance scheme that facilitates bank loans to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, and women entrepreneurs for setting up new (greenfield) enterprises in manufacturing, services, agri-allied, or trading sectors, promoting economic inclusion and entrepreneurship among underrepresented groups.
eligibility: SC or ST individual entrepreneur, or a woman entrepreneur, aged 18 years or above. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur. The loan is available only for a greenfield project — the applicant's first venture in the relevant sector. The borrower must not be in default to any bank or financial institution.
benefits: Composite bank loan (term loan + working capital) of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore per enterprise. The loan is expected to cover up to 85% of the project cost. Interest rate is the bank's lowest applicable rate for the category (not exceeding MCLR + 3% + tenure premium). Repayment period of up to 7 years with a maximum moratorium of 18 months.
documents: Identity proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport, etc.)
Bank account details and last 6 months' bank statements
No-objection certificate / trade licence as applicable
steps: Check eligibility and use the Loan Application Navigator at standupmitra.in
Prepare a detailed project report for your proposed greenfield enterprise
Apply online through the Stand-Up Mitra portal or approach the nearest scheduled bank branch directly
The bank appraises the application and project report
On sanction, the composite loan (term loan + working capital) is disbursed
Track your application status on the Stand-Up Mitra portal
source: Ministry of Finance / SIDBI / Stand-Up Mitra Portal

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
summary: A Ministry of Food Processing Industries centrally sponsored scheme to provide financial, technical, and business support for setting up or upgrading micro food processing enterprises across India, with a focus on the One District One Product (ODOP) approach.
eligibility: Existing micro food processing enterprises (individual proprietors, SHGs, co-operatives, FPOs, and producer companies) engaged in food processing. The applicant enterprise must typically have an annual turnover of up to ₹25 lakh and fewer than 10 workers. Individual applicants for credit-linked subsidy should own or lease the processing unit. The scheme prioritises ODOP-identified food products for each district.
benefits: Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of the eligible project cost, with a maximum ceiling of ₹10 lakh per individual enterprise (minimum 10% contribution by the beneficiary). For SHGs, seed capital of ₹4 lakh per SHG (₹40,000 per member) is available for working capital and purchase of small tools. Support for branding, packaging, and marketing. Technical and business capacity-building support.
documents: Aadhaar/identity proof of the proprietor or applicant
Proof of ownership or lease of the food processing unit
Project report covering the proposed upgrade/setup
Registration/licensing documents (FSSAI, GST, Udyam, as applicable)
steps: Visit pmfme.mofpi.gov.in for scheme details, ODOP product list, and application guidelines
Register on the PMFME portal as an individual or group applicant
Prepare a project report for the proposed food processing unit upgrade or setup
Submit the application online along with required documents
Application is appraised by the District Resource Person (DRP) and the State Nodal Agency
On approval, the subsidy is disbursed through the bank as a credit-linked back-end subsidy after loan disbursement
source: Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI), Government of India / PMFME Portal

name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM)
summary: A voluntary and contributory pension scheme for workers in the unorganised sector, ensuring a minimum monthly pension of ₹3,000 after the age of 60, providing financial security in old age to domestic workers, construction workers, street vendors, rag pickers, agricultural labourers, and similar workers.
eligibility: Unorganised sector workers aged 18 to 40 years with a monthly income of ₹15,000 or less. The worker should not be a member of EPFO, ESIC, or NPS, should not be an income tax payer, and should have a savings bank account and Aadhaar. Workers already registered on the e-Shram portal can link their PM-SYM enrolment.
benefits: Minimum assured pension of ₹3,000 per month after attaining age 60. If the subscriber dies after pension commencement, the spouse receives 50% of the pension as a family pension. The contribution is matched equally by the Central Government: for example, a worker joining at age 29 contributes ₹100 per month and the government contributes an equal ₹100 per month into the Pension Fund.
documents: Savings bank account passbook (with IFSC code)
Mobile number (for OTP verification at CSC)
steps: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar card and savings bank passbook
The CSC operator will complete the enrolment on the PM-SYM portal (maandhan.in)
Choose the monthly contribution amount based on your age of entry
Auto-debit of monthly contribution from your savings account is set up
Contributions are made monthly until age 60
On turning 60, apply for pension through the LIC branch linked to your account; pension is credited monthly to your bank account
source: Ministry of Labour and Employment / LIC of India / PM-SYM Portal

name: e-Shram — National Database of Unorganised Workers
summary: A Ministry of Labour and Employment portal to register unorganised workers and create a National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW). Registration provides workers with a Universal Account Number (UAN) card (e-Shram card) that serves as a portable identity and enables convergence of social security benefits.
eligibility: Any unorganised worker (home-based worker, self-employed, or wage worker in the unorganised sector, including workers in the organised sector not covered by ESIC or EPFO) aged 16 to 59 years. The worker should not be an income tax payer and should not be a member of ESIC or EPFO. An Aadhaar number and an Aadhaar-linked active mobile number are required.
benefits: A 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) and an e-Shram card that serves as a lifelong portable identity for the worker. Facilitates seamless delivery of social security and welfare benefits from central and state governments. Registered workers may be included in priority beneficiary lists for various schemes (PMSBY accident insurance, livelihood support, etc.) subject to current government notifications.
documents: Aadhaar-linked and active mobile number (for OTP verification)
Bank account number and IFSC code
steps: Visit eshram.gov.in or the Umang app, or go to the nearest CSC
Click 'Register on e-Shram' and enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number
Verify with the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile
Fill in personal, occupation, and bank account details
Submit the form — a 12-digit UAN is generated immediately
Download or collect your e-Shram card for use as a portable identity document
source: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India / e-Shram Portal

name: MeriPehchaan — National Single Sign-On
summary: A Digital India initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) that provides a single set of login credentials for citizens to access multiple government online portals and services — eliminating the need to create separate usernames and passwords for each government application.
eligibility: Any citizen of India who uses government online services can register for a MeriPehchaan account. There is no age, income, or category restriction. A valid mobile number and email address are required for registration.
benefits: One login for multiple government services and portals that have adopted MeriPehchaan (NSSO). Reduces the hassle of managing multiple credentials. Secure and centralised authentication for government applications. Supports the Digital India vision of seamless citizen-government interaction.
documents: Aadhaar number (optional, for stronger verification on some services)
steps: Visit meripehchaan.gov.in
Click 'Register' and enter your mobile number, email address, and basic details
Verify your mobile number with the OTP sent
Set a password to complete account creation
Use your MeriPehchaan credentials to log in to any participating government portal that displays the MeriPehchaan sign-in option
Manage your account and linked services from the MeriPehchaan dashboard
source: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India / MeriPehchaan Portal

name: Sanchar Saathi
summary: A Department of Telecommunications (DoT) citizen-centric portal and mobile app that empowers mobile phone users to check SIM connections registered in their name, report and block lost or stolen mobile phones, and verify the genuineness of mobile handsets before purchase.
eligibility: Any person holding a valid Indian mobile number can use the Sanchar Saathi portal or app. No registration, income criteria, or special eligibility is required for most services — just a mobile number for OTP verification.
benefits: Check the number of mobile connections registered in your name (TAFCOP) and request disconnection of connections you did not take or no longer need. Block a lost or stolen mobile phone using IMEI to prevent misuse (CEIR service). Trace the status of a blocked mobile phone. Verify whether a second-hand or new mobile handset is genuine and not blacklisted or duplicated before purchase. All services are free of charge.
documents: Valid Indian mobile number (for OTP-based verification)
FIR / police complaint number (required when reporting a lost or stolen phone)
IMEI number of the lost or stolen handset (printed on the device packaging or checked by dialling *#06#)
steps: Visit sancharsaathi.gov.in or download the Sanchar Saathi mobile app
To check your SIM connections: go to TAFCOP, enter your mobile number, verify with OTP, and view all connections in your name
To request disconnection of an unrecognised number: select it in TAFCOP and raise a disconnection request
To block a lost/stolen phone: go to CEIR, file an FIR first at the nearest police station, then submit the FIR number and IMEI on the portal
To check handset genuineness: use the 'Know Your Mobile' feature and enter the device's IMEI number
Track the status of your blocking request through the CEIR section of the portal
source: Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India

name: Bhashini — National Language Translation Mission
summary: A MeitY initiative under the Digital India Corporation that builds a National Public Digital Platform for AI-powered language technology across India's languages. Bhashini enables citizens to access digital services, government information, and content in their own language — through text, speech, and translation — breaking language barriers and promoting digital inclusion.
eligibility: Bhashini's services are available to all citizens regardless of language, education, or location. The Bhashini app and web platform are freely accessible. Developers and organisations can access APIs to integrate language services into their own applications. No income or category restriction applies.
benefits: Speech-to-text (voice input), text-to-speech (voice output), and translation in 22 Indian languages and English. Ability to read, listen to, and interact with government services and digital content in your preferred Indian language. Powers translations on 500+ government websites. Supports accessibility for non-English speakers and those with limited literacy. Free access through the Bhashini app (bhashini.ai) and web platform.
documents: No documents are required to use the Bhashini app or web platform
Developers/organisations integrating APIs should register on the Bhashini developer portal at bhashini.gov.in
steps: Download the Bhashini app from bhashini.ai, or visit bhashini.gov.in
Select your preferred language from the supported Indian languages
Use voice input (speech-to-text) to speak in your language and get text output
Use the translation feature to convert text or speech between supported Indian languages and English
Use text-to-speech to listen to content in your language
Developers and government agencies can register at bhashini.gov.in to integrate language AI APIs into their services
source: Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) / Digital India Corporation / MeitY, Government of India

name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY 4.0)
tags: Skills & Training • Unemployed Youth / School Dropouts
summary: The flagship skill training program by MSDE that provides free, industry-aligned short-term courses, certification, and post-placement support.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen aged 15–45 who is unemployed or looking for skill development.
benefits: 100% free technical and soft skill training. Government-recognized certification. Assessment. Placement support.
documents: Bank passbook / account details (linked with Aadhaar)
steps: Visit the Skill India Digital / PMKVY portal
Search for accredited training centers in your district
Register your candidate profile using Aadhaar
Select your preferred job role/course and enroll
Attend training, complete the final assessment, and receive certification
source: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship / PMKVY Portal

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) – Shishu, Kishore & Tarun
tags: Business Credit • Micro-Enterprises & Traders • Young Entrepreneurs
summary: Non-farm, non-corporate micro-loans providing structured financial backing across growth stages with zero collateral requirements.
eligibility: Indian citizens running or setting up revenue-generating micro-enterprises in manufacturing, trading, or service sectors without existing loan defaults. Any Indian citizen aged 18 or above with a viable business plan for a non-farm revenue-generating activity.
benefits: Shishu: up to ₹50,000. Kishore: ₹50,001 to ₹5 Lakh. Tarun: ₹5 Lakh to ₹10 Lakh. Tarun Plus: up to ₹20 Lakh. No processing fees. Affordable interest rates. Zero collateral requirements.
documents: Quotation of machinery/tools to be purchased or business estimate
Bank account statement for the past 6 months
steps: Prepare your business proposal and itemized cost breakdown
Apply through the unified JanSamarth portal or visit your preferred bank branch
Select the appropriate MUDRA loan category based on funding needs (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun)
Submit your KYC and project cost documents for bank appraisal
Receive loan sanction and MUDRA debit card for working capital withdrawals
source: Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency (MUDRA) / Ministry of Finance / JanSamarth Portal

name: PM-YASASVI Central Sector Scholarship
tags: Education & Scholarship • OBC, EBC & DNT Students
summary: Comprehensive scholarship scheme by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment for meritorious Other Backward Class, EBC, and DNT students.
eligibility: Students belonging to OBC, EBC, or Non-Creamy Layer DNT categories whose annual family income is below ₹2.5 lakh, studying in designated top-class schools or colleges.
benefits: Full tuition fee support. Living expenses. Stationery/computer grant allowances paid directly to the bank account.
documents: Aadhaar Card & Student Bank Account Details
Fee receipt and college bonafide certificate
steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal (NSP)
Complete OTR (One Time Registration) with Aadhaar
Select PM-YASASVI from the scheme directory
Upload income, caste, and academic verification documents
Submit application for institute-level verification
source: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment / National Scholarship Portal

name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
summary: Financial assistance to early-stage student and youth entrepreneurs for proof of concept, prototype development, and market entry.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognized startup incorporated within 2 years, having a viable product idea with market fit, with Indian founders holding at least 51% stake.
benefits: Up to ₹20 lakh grant for validation of Proof of Concept and prototype development. Up to ₹50 lakh via debt/convertible debentures for commercialization.
steps: Register company on the Startup India portal and apply for DPIIT recognition
Login to the Seed Fund Scheme portal
Choose and apply to up to 3 sector-relevant incubators across India
Present your pitch during incubator evaluation sessions
source: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) / Startup India

name: Agnipath Scheme
tags: Defense & National Service • Armed Forces Aspirants
summary: A recruitment model providing Indian youth an opportunity to serve in the Indian Armed Forces as Agniveers for a four-year tenure.
eligibility: Unmarried Indian male/female candidates aged between 17.5 and 21 years with 10th or 12th pass qualifications meeting medical fitness benchmarks.
benefits: Customized monthly salary package (starting ₹30,000 progressing to ₹40,000). ₹48 lakh life cover. Tax-free Seva Nidhi package of approximately ₹11.71 lakh upon release.
documents: Class 10/12 educational marksheets and passing certificates
NCC / Sports certificates (if claiming bonus marks)
steps: Register on the official branch portal (Join Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force)
Complete online exam registration when rally dates are published
Appear for Computer-Based Common Entrance Exam (CEE)
Attend physical fitness test (PFT), physical measurement, and medical tests
source: Ministry of Defence / Indian Armed Forces / Join Indian Army Portal

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
summary: Credit guarantee coverage enabling micro and small enterprises to secure bank credit for term loans and working capital without third-party collateral.
eligibility: New and existing Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) engaged in manufacturing, services, or select trading activities.
benefits: Third-party guarantee coverage for institutional credit facilities up to ₹5 Crore per eligible unit, removing property mortgage barriers.
documents: Detailed Project Report (DPR) with business viability projections
Company PAN, GST registration, and Incorporation papers
Audited or provisional financial balance sheets
steps: Register your business unit on the Udyam portal
Prepare an enterprise proposal covering working capital and machinery requirements
Approach a CGTMSE-member lending institution (Public/Private Bank or NBFC)
Request the bank to sanction the facility under CGTMSE guarantee cover
Bank conducts appraisal and secures direct guarantee cover from the trust
source: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) / MSME

name: Udyam Registration (Zero-Cost MSME Portal)
tags: Business Formalization • Small Business Owners & Vendors
summary: The official government registration portal to classify enterprises as Micro, Small, or Medium, unlocking statutory MSME benefits and protections.
eligibility: Any business entity or proprietorship engaged in manufacturing or services meeting the MSME investment and turnover thresholds.
benefits: Permanent Udyam registration number. Statutory protection against delayed payments from buyers. Priority sector lending access. Lower trademark registration fees.
documents: Aadhaar Card of the proprietor/managing director
GSTIN (if turnover requires mandatory GST registration)
steps: Navigate to the official Udyam Registration portal
Authenticate the proprietor/promoter's Aadhaar via OTP
Enter PAN details and enterprise location data
Enter plant/equipment investment values and turnover figures
Submit the self-declaration to instantly generate your Udyam Certificate
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) / Udyam Registration Portal

name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)
summary: Financial assistance to organize traditional artisans and rural craft makers into competitive clusters with modern machinery and market access.
eligibility: Non-Government Organizations (NGOs), cooperatives, producer companies, and Panchayati Raj Institutions representing groups of traditional artisans.
benefits: Grants up to ₹2.5 Crore for Regular Clusters (up to 500 artisans). Grants up to ₹5 Crore for Major Clusters. Development of Common Facility Centres (CFCs) and product branding.
documents: Detailed Project Proposal for cluster development
Roster of enrolled artisans with Aadhaar details
Land allotment or long-term lease papers for the Common Facility Centre
steps: Implementing agency prepares a diagnostic study and preliminary concept note
Submit the proposal online through the SFURTI MIS portal
Presentation before the Scheme Steering Committee (SSC)
Appointment of Technical Agency (TA) and preparation of DPR
Fund release in phases for civil works, machinery installation, and market linkages
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) / SFURTI Portal

name: MSME Champions Scheme – ZED Certification Component
summary: Encourages micro and small manufacturers to adopt Zero Defect, Zero Effect practices to boost product quality and environmental standards.
eligibility: All manufacturing micro, small, and medium enterprises holding a valid Udyam Registration.
benefits: Subsidies on certification costs: up to 80% for Micro units, up to 60% for Small units, up to 50% for Medium units. Bonus financial support for clean energy adoption.
documents: Factory layout and process flow chart
Quality control records and safety compliance logs
steps: Register on the MSME ZED portal using your Udyam ID
Take the free ZED Pledge to demonstrate quality commitment
Complete internal desktop assessment and upload compliance documentation
Undergo physical or remote site audit by an accredited agency
Receive ZED Bronze, Silver, or Gold Certification along with financial reimbursement
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) / ZED Portal

name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) – Technology Upgradation
summary: Upfront capital subsidy for micro and small industrial units to upgrade traditional manufacturing processes with modern technology.
eligibility: Existing MSE units upgrading plant machinery or newly established units installing state-of-the-art eligible technologies.
benefits: 15% upfront capital subsidy (on institutional credit up to ₹1 Crore) for procuring approved modern machinery and automation systems.
documents: Equipment supplier proforma invoice and technical specs
Term loan sanction letter from commercial bank
Audited financial statements of preceding three years
steps: Identify approved plant machinery required for manufacturing modernization
Apply for a machinery term loan through an empanelled primary lending institution
Bank uploads the subsidy application to the online CLCSS portal
Verification by nodal agencies (SIDBI/NABARD)
Direct subsidy release credited into borrower's term loan reserve account
source: Development Commissioner for Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (DC MSME)

name: GeM – Government e-Marketplace Direct Vendor Onboarding
tags: B2G Commerce • Local Suppliers & Direct Vendors
summary: End-to-end national procurement portal connecting micro-vendors, retailers, and suppliers directly with central and state government procurement officers.
eligibility: Registered proprietorships, partnerships, retailers, or manufacturing entities holding a PAN and active bank account.
benefits: Direct access to over ₹2+ Lakh Crore of public procurement without middlemen. Mandatory 25% quota reservations. Zero tender-fee exemptions for MSMEs.
documents: Active bank account and cancelled cheque
steps: Visit the GeM official portal and initiate Seller Registration
Authenticate the key person via Aadhaar and PAN verification
Complete business profile, store address, and bank linkage
Upload your product catalog or service offerings with pricing
Participate in direct purchases, L1 bids, and national government e-tenders
source: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) / Ministry of Commerce and Industry

name: National SC/ST Hub (NSSH) Scheme
summary: Specialized capability building and vendor development initiative to help SC/ST entrepreneurs fulfill public procurement mandates.
eligibility: Micro and Small enterprises owned by Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe promoters (at least 51% stake).
benefits: Subsidized participation in domestic and international expos. 100% subsidy for single-point vendor registration with NSIC. Specialized vendor development clinics.
documents: Caste Certificate of the primary promoter
steps: Register on the official National SC-ST Hub portal
Link your Udyam Certificate showing SC/ST ownership classification
Attend vendor development training sessions organized by Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)
Apply for reimbursement of testing, quality certification, and stall fees
source: National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) / National SC/ST Hub

name: SIDBI SMILE – Make in India Soft Loan Fund for MSMEs
tags: Growth & Expansion • Established Micro & Small Units
summary: Quasi-equity soft loans and term loan assistance to help small enterprises meet debt-equity ratios for technology and capacity expansion.
eligibility: Micro and small businesses operating in designated Make in India manufacturing and services sectors for at least 3 years.
benefits: Soft loans in the form of quasi-equity to cover promoter contribution gaps. Term loans with lower interest rates. Moratoriums up to 36 months.
documents: Audited financial statements for the past 3 fiscal years
Detailed Project Report detailing plant expansion or machinery purchase
steps: Register on the SIDBI borrower portal
Submit your project requirements under the SMILE scheme category
Upload past financial track record and projected cash flows
Attend techno-economic viability evaluation with SIDBI credit officers
Direct loan sanction and disbursement aligned with project milestones
source: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
summary: Grant-in-aid for creating Common Facility Centres (CFCs) and developing modern infrastructure in new and existing industrial estates.
eligibility: Groups of micro and small enterprises, industrial associations, or SPVs operating within a concentrated geographic cluster.
benefits: Up to 70% to 80% central grant assistance (up to ₹30 Crore) for testing centers, common training facilities, effluent plants, and road/power networks.
documents: Detailed Project Report (DPR) of the Common Facility Centre
steps: Form an SPV consisting of local cluster business units
Prepare DPR for the required common facility (testing lab, cold storage, machining shop)
Submit application online through the MSE-CDP portal
State Level Steering Committee (SLSC) appraisal and MoMSME clearance
Staged release of central grant for infrastructure development
source: Development Commissioner for Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (DC MSME) / MSE-CDP Portal

name: MSME Samadhaan – Delayed Payment Monitoring System
summary: Statutory dispute resolution mechanism empowering micro and small enterprises to recover delayed payments from corporate and government buyers.
eligibility: Micro and small businesses registered under Udyam that supplied goods or services with unpaid invoices exceeding 45 days.
benefits: Mandatory compounding interest payable by defaulters at three times the RBI bank rate on overdue amounts, enforced by the statutory Facilitation Council (MSEFC).
documents: Purchase Order (PO) issued by the buyer
Delivery challan / proof of service delivery
Copy of unpaid invoices with payment reminder communication
steps: Log in to the MSME Samadhaan portal using Udyam credentials
File a delayed payment case against the buyer
Upload supporting invoices and delivery receipts
Micro & Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC) issues statutory notices
Mutually conciliated settlement or binding arbitration decree issued to recover dues
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) / Samadhaan Portal

name: ASPIRE – Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industry & Entrepreneurship
summary: Sets up Livelihood Business Incubators (LBIs) and Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) across rural districts to train young village entrepreneurs.
eligibility: Any youth, aspiring vendor, or micro-entrepreneur seeking practical operational training to start small agricultural or processing ventures.
benefits: Practical hands-on training with modern machinery. Incubation space. Enterprise guidance. Direct links to financial schemes like PMEGP and MUDRA.
documents: Application to local district Livelihood Business Incubator
steps: Locate the nearest ASPIRE Livelihood Business Incubator in your district
Select your agro-processing or light manufacturing training trade
Complete training on commercial-grade machinery
Receive mentor support to draft a business project report
Apply for enterprise seed credit to establish your commercial unit
source: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) / ASPIRE Portal

name: TReDS – Trade Receivables Discounting System
summary: An institutional electronic auction platform where micro and small enterprise suppliers discount unpaid trade invoices through competitive bank bidding.
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises supplying goods or services to large corporates, CPSEs, or government departments.
benefits: Immediate liquidity within 48 to 72 hours without waiting for standard 90-day buyer credit terms. No personal collateral required.
documents: Delivery challan signed by the buyer
Bank account and GST registration details
steps: Register as a seller on any RBI-approved TReDS platform (RXIL, M1xchange, or Invoicemart)
Upload valid buyer-accepted tax invoices on the platform
Buyer digitally validates and approves the invoice on the portal
Financiers (banks/factors) bid competitive discount rates on the accepted invoice
Accept the best bid and receive the net funds directly in your bank account
source: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) / RXIL TReDS Platform
